subject: math
title: Telling Time to the Nearest 5 Minutes
seo_title: Grade 2 Telling Time Worksheets: Nearest 5 Minutes, Half Hour, Quarter Hour, a.m. and p.m.
standard_text: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 telling time worksheets with clock pictures: o'clock and half past, counting by 5s around the clock, reading the clock to the nearest 5 minutes, quarter past and quarter to, and a.m. or p.m. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Short hand = hour. Long hand = minutes: count by 5s from the 12.
key_sub: Each number is 5 minutes for the long hand, so the 4 means 20 minutes. If the short hand is between two numbers, use the number it just passed. a.m. is the morning; p.m. is the afternoon and evening.
body_html:
The big idea

A clock has two hands. The short hand tells the hour. The long hand tells the minutes. Read the short hand first, then the long hand.

  1. Hour: look at the short hand. If it is between two numbers, use the number it just passed.
  2. Minutes: look at the long hand. Count by 5s from the 12 to the long hand.
  3. Write it: hour, a colon, then two digits for the minutes: 4:35, 9:05, 6:00.

Count by 5s around the clock

Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand. Start at the 12 and count by 5s.

Long hand on121234567891011
Minutes0510152025303540455055
WordsTimeLong hand on
7 o'clock7:0012
quarter past 77:153
half past 77:306
quarter to 87:459
Example

The short hand is between 9 and 10. The long hand is on the 4. What time is it?

The hour is 9. Count by 5s to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20.

Answer: 9:20

a.m. and p.m.

Each day the clock goes around two times. a.m. is from midnight to noon: the night and the morning. p.m. is from noon to midnight: the afternoon and the evening.

TimeWhat you might do
7:00 a.m.eat breakfast
10:30 a.m.play at recess
3:15 p.m.go home from school
6:00 p.m.eat dinner
8:30 p.m.go to bed
Example

Mia's dance class starts at 3:30 p.m. It lasts 1 hour. When does it end?

In 1 hour the hour goes up by 1. The minutes stay the same. It is still the afternoon.

Answer: 4:30 p.m.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Switching the hands (reading 4:35 as 7:20)Short hand = hour. Long hand = minutes
Reading the long hand on 4 as 4 minutes (3:04)Count by 5s: the 4 means 20 minutes, so it is 3:20
Reading 2:50 as 3:50 because the short hand is near the 3If the short hand has not reached a number, use the number before it
Eating dinner at 6:00 a.m.Morning is a.m. Afternoon and evening are p.m.

faq.q: What should a 2nd grader know about telling time?
faq.a: By the end of Grade 2, children tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks, and use a.m. and p.m. Telling time to the exact minute and finding elapsed time come in Grade 3.

faq.q: How do I teach my child to count by 5s on a clock?
faq.a: Point to each number on the clock and count 5, 10, 15 … from the 12. The long hand on the 4 means 20 minutes, and on the 9 means 45 minutes.

faq.q: Why is the hour hand between two numbers?
faq.a: The hour hand moves slowly all hour. At 7:35 it has left the 7 but not reached the 8, so the hour is still 7.

faq.q: How do you explain a.m. and p.m. to a child?
faq.a: a.m. is from midnight to noon, like breakfast at 7:00 a.m. p.m. is from noon to midnight, like dinner at 6:00 p.m.

items.e: The short hand points to the 5. The long hand points to the 12. That means it is 5 o'clock: 5:00.
The long hand points to the 6. That is 30 minutes, half of the way around. The short hand is halfway between 11 and 12, so the hour is still 11. It is 11:30, half past 11.
The short hand points to the 7. The long hand points to the 12. That means it is 7 o'clock: 7:00.
The long hand points to the 6. That is 30 minutes, half of the way around. The short hand is halfway between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. It is 12:30, half past 12.
The short hand points to the 8. The long hand points to the 12. That means it is 8 o'clock: 8:00.
The long hand points to the 6. That is 30 minutes, half of the way around. The short hand is halfway between 4 and 5, so the hour is still 4. It is 4:30, half past 4.
The short hand points to the 1. The long hand points to the 12. That means it is 1 o'clock: 1:00.
The long hand points to the 6. That is 30 minutes, half of the way around. The short hand is halfway between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. It is 9:30, half past 9.
Half past 5 means 30 minutes after 5 o'clock. That is 5:30.
2 o'clock means the hour is 2 and there are 0 minutes. Write it as 2:00.
30 minutes after 6 o'clock is half past 6.
The minutes are :00, so it is right on the hour: 6 o'clock.

items.q: At 9:00, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At an o'clock time the long hand always points straight up to the 12. The short hand points to the 9.

items.q: At 2:30, where does the long hand point?
items.e: 30 minutes is half of the way around the clock. The long hand points to the 6. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. (It is not the 3. The 3 means 15 minutes.)

items.q: At 7:30, where is the short hand?
items.e: In 30 minutes the short hand moves halfway to the next number. At 7:30 it is halfway between 7 and 8.

items.q: At 11:00, where is the short hand?
items.e: At 11 o'clock the short hand points right on the 11. The long hand is on the 12.

items.q: It is 3:00. What time will it be in half an hour?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. The long hand moves from the 12 to the 6. 3:00 + 30 minutes = 3:30.

items.q: It is 3:30. What time will it be in half an hour?
items.e: 30 more minutes takes the long hand from the 6 back up to the 12. That is the next hour: 4:00.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: The long hand goes all the way around the clock in 1 hour. Count by 5s to the 12: 60 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 3: 5, 10, 15. So it is 15 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 7: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So it is 35 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 2: 5, 10. So it is 10 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 9: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. So it is 45 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 11: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55. So it is 55 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. So it is 25 minutes.
Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 8: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. So it is 40 minutes.

items.q: The long hand is on the 1. How many minutes after the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. The 1 is the first number after the 12, so it is 5 minutes.

items.q: The long hand is on the 6. How many minutes after the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 6: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So it is 30 minutes.

items.q: The long hand is on the 10. How many minutes after the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 10: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. So it is 50 minutes.

items.q: The long hand is on the 4. How many minutes after the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 minutes.

items.q: The long hand is on the 8. How many minutes after the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 8: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. So it is 40 minutes.

items.q: The long hand is on the 11. How many minutes after the hour is it?
items.e: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s to the 11: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55. So it is 55 minutes.

items.q: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 3. How many minutes go by?
items.e: Count by 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15. 15 minutes go by.

items.q: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 8. How many minutes go by?
items.e: Count by 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. 40 minutes go by.

items.q: The long hand goes all the way around, from the 12 back to the 12. How much time goes by?
items.e: 12 numbers × 5 minutes = 60 minutes. 60 minutes is 1 hour.

items.q: It is 10 minutes after the hour. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5 is the 1, 10 is the 2. (The 10 on the clock means 50 minutes.)

items.q: It is 40 minutes after the hour. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: Count by 5s until you say 40: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. That is 8 numbers, so the long hand is on the 8.

items.q: It is 55 minutes after the hour. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: 55 is 5 minutes before the hour, one number before the 12. The long hand is on the 11.
The short hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is 12. The long hand points to the 1. Count by 5s: 5. It is 12:05.
The short hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is 8. The long hand points to the 2. Count by 5s: 5, 10. It is 8:10.
The short hand is between 10 and 11, so the hour is 10. The long hand points to the 3. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. It is 10:15.
The short hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is 2. The long hand points to the 4. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 2:20.
The short hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is 8. The long hand points to the 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 8:25.
The short hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is 1. The long hand points to the 7. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. It is 1:35.
The short hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is 7. The long hand points to the 1. Count by 5s: 5. It is 7:05.
The short hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is 1. The long hand points to the 2. Count by 5s: 5, 10. It is 1:10.
The short hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is 11. The long hand points to the 4. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. It is 11:20.
The short hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is 6. The long hand points to the 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It is 6:25.
The short hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is 8. The long hand points to the 7. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. It is 8:35.
The short hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is 4. The long hand points to the 3. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. It is 4:15.
The short hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is 9. It is almost at the 10, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 8. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. It is 9:40.
The short hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is 3. It is almost at the 4, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 9. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. It is 3:45.

The short hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is 7. It is almost at the 8, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 10. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. It is 7:50.

The short hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is 11. It is almost at the 12, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 11. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55. It is 11:55.
The short hand is between 10 and 11, so the hour is 10. It is almost at the 11, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 8. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. It is 10:40.
The short hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is 4. It is almost at the 5, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 9. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. It is 4:45.

The short hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is 2. It is almost at the 3, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 10. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. It is 2:50.

The short hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is 5. It is almost at the 6, but it has not got there yet. The long hand points to the 11. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55. It is 5:55.

sets.title: Match clocks, quarter hours and the short hand

items.e: In Clock A the short hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is 1. The long hand is on the 7: count by 5s to 35. Clock A shows 1:35. Clock B has the hands switched.
In Clock B the short hand is between 4 and 5, so the hour is 4. The long hand is on the 2: count by 5s to 10. Clock B shows 4:10. Clock A has the hands switched.
In Clock C the short hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is 2. The long hand is on the 10: count by 5s to 50. Clock C shows 2:50. Clock B has the hands switched.
In Clock D the short hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is 9. The long hand is on the 5: count by 5s to 25. Clock D shows 9:25. Clock C has the hands switched.
In Clock B the short hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is 5. The long hand is on the 8: count by 5s to 40. Clock B shows 5:40. Clock D has the hands switched.
In Clock C the short hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is 11. The long hand is on the 3: count by 5s to 15. Clock C shows 11:15. Clock B has the hands switched.

items.q: This digital clock shows 4:50. On a clock with hands, where does the long hand point?
items.e: The minutes are 50. Count by 5s until you say 50: that is 10 numbers. The long hand points to the 10. (The 5 on the clock means 25 minutes.)

items.q: This digital clock shows 9:20. On a clock with hands, where does the long hand point?
items.e: The minutes are 20. Count by 5s until you say 20: that is 4 numbers. The long hand points to the 4. (The 2 on the clock means 10 minutes.)

items.q: This digital clock shows 11:35. On a clock with hands, where does the long hand point?
items.e: The minutes are 35. Count by 5s until you say 35: that is 7 numbers. The long hand points to the 7. (The 3 on the clock means 15 minutes.)

items.q: This digital clock shows 6:45. On a clock with hands, where does the long hand point?
items.e: The minutes are 45. Count by 5s until you say 45: that is 9 numbers. The long hand points to the 9. (The 4 on the clock means 20 minutes.)
A quarter hour is 15 minutes. Quarter past 2 means 15 minutes after 2 o'clock: 2:15.
Quarter to 10 means 15 minutes before 10 o'clock. 15 minutes before 10:00 is 9:45.
The long hand is on the 3: that is 15 minutes, a quarter of the way around. The short hand is just past the 8. It is 8:15, quarter past 8.
The clock shows 10:45. In 15 more minutes it will be 11 o'clock, so 10:45 is quarter to 11.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter hour?
items.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts. The long hand moves from the 12 to the 3: 15 minutes. (A quarter coin is 25 cents, but a quarter hour is 15 minutes.)

items.q: It is 3:35. Where is the short hand?
items.e: The short hand moves a little as the minutes go by. At 3:35 it has left the 3 but has not reached the 4. It is between 3 and 4.

items.q: It is 1:20. Where is the short hand?
items.e: The short hand moves a little as the minutes go by. At 1:20 it has left the 1 but has not reached the 2. It is between 1 and 2.

items.q: At 2:50, which number is the short hand closest to?
items.e: At 2:50 it is almost 3 o'clock. The short hand is between 2 and 3, very close to the 3. (The long hand is the one on the 10.)

items.q: At 8:10, which number is the short hand closest to?
items.e: At 8:10 the hour has just started. The short hand is just past the 8. (The long hand is the one on the 2.)
The short hand has not reached the 5 yet, so the hour is still 4. The long hand is on the 11: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes. It is 4:55. In 5 more minutes it will be 5:00.

sets.title: Times of day: a.m., p.m. and later times

items.q: Eli eats breakfast before school. What time could it be?
items.e: Breakfast is in the morning, so it is an a.m. time: 7:15 a.m.

items.q: Owen wakes up for school. What time could it be?
items.e: Waking up for school happens in the morning. Morning times are a.m.: 6:45 a.m.

items.q: School starts. What time could it be?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is a.m.: 8:05 a.m. (3:05 a.m. is the middle of the night.)

items.q: Nora plays outside at morning recess. What time could it be?
items.e: Morning recess is during the school day, before noon. That is a.m.: 10:20 a.m.

items.q: Ava rides the bus home from school. What time could it be?
items.e: School ends in the afternoon. Afternoon times are p.m.: 3:10 p.m.

items.q: Jack eats a snack after school. What time could it be?
items.e: After school is the afternoon. Afternoon times are p.m.: 3:45 p.m.

items.q: Leo eats dinner with his family. What time could it be?
items.e: Dinner is in the evening. Evening times are p.m.: 6:00 p.m.

items.q: Noah goes to bed at night. What time could it be?
items.e: Going to bed happens at night, after noon and before midnight. That is p.m.: 8:30 p.m.

items.q: Sofia is fast asleep. It is the middle of the night. What time could it be?
items.e: After midnight a new day starts, and the times are a.m. The middle of the night is a time like 2:00 a.m.

items.q: It is 9:00 p.m. What is Omar most likely doing?
items.e: 9:00 p.m. is late in the evening, so Omar is most likely sleeping. At 9:00 a.m. he would be at school.

items.q: It is 7:00 a.m. What is Emma most likely doing?
items.e: 7:00 a.m. is early in the morning, before school, so Emma is most likely eating breakfast. Dinner and bedtime are p.m.

items.q: It is 4:15. What time will it be in 1 hour?
items.e: In 1 hour the short hand moves to the next number. The minutes stay the same. 4:15 → 5:15. (4:16 is only 1 minute later.)
The clock shows 2:40. In 1 hour the hour goes up by 1 and the minutes stay the same: 3:40.

items.q: It is 2:10. What time will it be in 30 minutes?
items.e: Count on by 5s from the 2: 30 minutes is 6 numbers. The long hand goes from the 2 to the 8. 2:10 → 2:40. (3:10 is 1 hour later, not 30 minutes.)

items.q: It is 9:45. What time will it be in 30 minutes?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes to 10:00, then 15 more minutes: 10:15. The long hand went past the 12, so the hour goes up to 10.

items.q: Luis's soccer practice starts at 4:30 p.m. It lasts 1 hour. What time does it end?
items.e: 1 hour after 4:30 is 5:30. It is still the afternoon, so it is 5:30 p.m.

items.q: Sam gets to the park at 10:15 a.m. He stays for 1 hour. What time does he leave?
items.e: 1 hour after 10:15 is 11:15. It is still before noon, so it is 11:15 a.m.

items.q: Zoe's piano lesson starts at 2:00 p.m. It lasts half an hour. What time does it end?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 2:00 + 30 minutes = 2:30 p.m. (2:15 is only a quarter hour later.)

items.q: Ben starts his homework at 3:40 p.m. He works for 30 minutes. What time does he finish?
items.e: Count on 20 minutes from 3:40 to 4:00. Then 10 more minutes: 4:10 p.m. The long hand went past the 12, so the hour changed from 3 to 4.

items.q: Lily's swim class starts at 5:45 p.m. It lasts 30 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes from 5:45 to 6:00. Then 15 more minutes: 6:15 p.m. (5:15 p.m. forgets that the hour changed.)
